data.content_ref: inline:Artifact 0bb6167c36cf contradicts SRC_002 by claiming that 'discrepancy-driven discovery' of unlisted variables is actually a signal of checklist failure (noise) rather than reliability gain; it argues that genuine reliability depends on the checklist's ability to constrain the panel to known failure modes. This is refuted if panels that identify unlisted errors show higher variance in final judgments than panels that adhere strictly to the prompt.
